'''''Desmodesmus''''' is a [[genus]] of [[green algae]] in the family [[Scenedesmaceae]].<ref>See the [[National Center for Biotechnology Information|NCBI]] [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Taxonomy/Browser/wwwtax.cgi?mode=Info&id=91202 webpage on Desmodesmus]. Data extracted from the {{cite web | url=https://ftp.ncbi.nih.gov/pub/taxonomy/ | title=NCBI taxonomy resources | publisher=[[National Center for Biotechnology Information]] | access-date=2007-03-19}}</ref>

==Morphology==
''Desmodesmus'' consists of colonies of two, four, eight or 16 cells arranged in a row. Cells are ellipsoidal to ovoid, joined to each other by their longer sides. The terminal cells of a colony (and sometimes the medial cells as well) are usually armed with spines. Cell walls may also be covered in ridges, warts, and net-like structures. Cells contain one parietal [[chloroplast]], containing one [[pyrenoid]].<ref name=Shubert2014>{{cite book |editor-first1=John D.|editor-last1=Wehr|editor-first2=Robert G.|editor-last2=Sheath|editor-first3=J. Patrick|editor-last3=Kociolek |date= 2014 |edition=2 |title= Freshwater Algae of North America: Ecology and Classification |last1= Shubert|first1=Elliot| last2=Gärtner |first2=Georg |chapter= Chapter 7. Nonmotile Coccoid and Colonial Green Algae |url= |location= |publisher= Elsevier Inc. |page= |isbn=978-0-12-385876-4 }}</ref>

''Desmodesmus'' species usually produce colonies of more than one cell, but single cells (unicells) may be found as well.<ref name=Lurling/> These single cells may be confused with ''[[Lagerheimia]]'', a genus of single-celled algae.<ref name=Bicudo_and_Menezes2006>{{cite book | title= Gêneros de Algas de Águas Continentais do Brasil: chave para identificação e descrições | edition=2 | year=2006 | first1=Carlos E. M. |last1=Bicudo | first2=Mariângela | last2= Menezes | publisher= RiMa Editora | pages=508 | isbn= 857656064X }}</ref>

The [[cell wall]] of ''Desmodesmus'' consists of an outer layer with a net-like structure, with "rosettes" of tubes underneath.<ref name=Hegewald/> These structures are not visible under [[light microscopy]], and only become visible under a [[scanning electron microscope]] (SEM) or [[transmission electron microscope]].<ref name=Shubert>{{cite journal | doi=10.5091/plecevo.2014.902 | title=An autoecological investigation of ''Desmodesmus'': Implications for ecology and taxonomy | date=2014 | last1=Shubert | first1=Elliot | last2=Wilk-Woźniak | first2=Elżbieta | last3=Ligęza | first3=Sławomir | journal=Plant Ecology and Evolution | volume=147 | issue=2 | pages=202–212 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Reproduction==
''Desmodesmus'' typically reproduces [[asexual reproduction|asexually]] by forming [[autospore]]s.<ref name=Lurling/> [[Sexual reproduction]] has been observed a few times.<ref name=Lurling/>

==Taxonomy==
Species in the genus ''Desmodesmus'' have long been placed in the related genus ''[[Scenedesmus]]''.<ref name=Lurling>{{cite journal|doi=10.1051/limn/2003014 |title=Phenotypic plasticity in the green algae ''Desmodesmus'' and ''Scenedesmus'' with special reference to the induction of defensive morphology |date=2003 |last1=Lürling |first1=M. |journal=Annales de Limnologie - International Journal of Limnology |volume=39 |issue=2 |pages=85–101 |doi-access=free }}</ref> However, ''Scenedesmus'' was found to be [[polyphyletic]], and was split up into several genera (corresponding to the subgenera within ''Scenedesmus''). ''Desmodesmus'' has ornamented cell walls, while ''Scenedesmus [[sensu stricto]]'' lacks ornamentation.<ref name=Shubert/>

A factor that has long complicated the taxonomy of ''Scenedesmus'' and its related taxa is the fact that these algae show considerable [[phenotypic plasticity]]. This plasticity has led taxonomists in the past to designate thousands of [[infraspecific name]]s based on minute changes in spine morphology or cell shape.<ref name=Lurling/> However, in laboratory conditions the same strain may produce an array of different morphologies.<ref name=Lurling/>

Currently, ''Desmodesmus'' species are delimited using a combination of [[ultrastructure|ultrastructural]] features and [[molecular data]]. In particular, the locus [[ITS-2]] provides enough variability to distinguish between species.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.2216/10-16.1 |title=Taxonomy of ''Desmodesmus serratus'' (Chlorophyceae, Chlorophyta) and related taxa on the basis of morphological and DNA sequence data |date=2011 |last1=Fawley |first1=Marvin W. |last2=Fawley |first2=Karen P. |last3=Hegewald |first3=Eberhard |journal=Phycologia |volume=50 |issue=1 |pages=23–56 |bibcode=2011Phyco..50...23F |s2cid=20900018 }}</ref>

==Habitat==
''Desmodesmus'' is found in the [[plankton]] of habitats such as ponds and lakes, particularly in [[eutrophic]] waters.<ref name=Hegewald>{{cite journal|doi=10.5507/fot.2017.001 |title=A taxonomic revision of ''Desmodesmus'' serie ''Desmodesmus'' (Sphaeropleales, Scenedesmaceae) |date=2017 |last1=Hegewald |first1=Eberhard |last2=Braband |first2=Anke |journal=Fottea |volume=17 |issue=2 |pages=191–208 |doi-access=free }}</ref> It is one of the most common types of freshwater plankton.<ref name=Shubert2014/> They can also be found in soils and [[biological soil crust]]s.<ref name=Johnson>{{cite journal | doi=10.2216/05-69.1 | title=The diversity of ''Scenedesmus'' and ''Desmodesmus'' (Chlorophyceae) in Itasca State Park, Minnesota, USA | date=2007 | last1=Johnson | first1=Joni L. | last2=Fawley | first2=Marvin W. | last3=Fawley | first3=Karen P. | journal=Phycologia | volume=46 | issue=2 | pages=214–229 | bibcode=2007Phyco..46..214J | s2cid=84448925 }}</ref>

==Ecology==
''Desmodesmus'' species tolerate a wide range of habitats and conditions; this also makes them easy to [[cell culture|culture]]. In response to [[herbivory]] from predators such as ''[[Daphnia]]'', ''Desmodesmus'' may develop spines or other defensive features.<ref name=Lurling/>

==Pathogenicity==
''Desmodesmus armatus'' is the only [[chlorophyll]]-containing organism confirmed to have caused human infections in [[immunocompetence|immunocompetent]] individuals.  All known cases involved open injuries occurring in fresh water.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Westblade|first1=Lars F.|last2=Ranganath|first2=Sangeetha|last3=Dunne|first3=William Michael|last4=Burnham|first4=Carey-Ann D.|author-link4=Carey-Ann Burnham|last5=Fader|first5=Robert|last6=Ford|first6=Bradley A.|date=2015-03-05|title=Infection with a Chlorophyllic Eukaryote after a Traumatic Freshwater Injury|journal=New England Journal of Medicine|volume=372|issue=10|pages=982–984|doi=10.1056/NEJMc1401816|issn=0028-4793|pmid=25738686|doi-access=free}}</ref> ''Desmodesmus'' is presumably a [[Mixotroph|mixotrophic]] organism (as are plenty of other genera of algae), obtaining most of its food [[Photosynthesis|photosynthetically]] but capable of [[Heterotroph|heterotrophy]] in unfavourable (poorly lit) conditions (such as within a deep puncture wound).

Non-photosynthesizing algae, on the other hand, have been long known to assume pathogenic roles, either facultatively or obligatorily. A well-studied example is [[Prototheca|''Prototheca.'']]
